app.name: Entrepreneurship Nexus
app.description: Shared data and coordination layer for regional entrepreneurial ecosystems: support organizations, founders, funders, referrals and program participation, with consent-gated sharing.

entrepreneur-support.title: Entrepreneur Support Networks
entrepreneur-support.definition: Vocabulary for regional networks that support founders and small businesses: the organizations in them (support organizations, funders, workspaces and the ventures they serve), the people involved, enrollment in programs, hand-offs between organizations, and the touchpoints and long-running work those organizations record.

concepts.definition: A business, nonprofit or agency taking part in a regional entrepreneurial network, whether it supports founders, funds them, hosts them, or is itself a venture being supported, carrying its roles in the network, tax status, industry, support it offers or needs, and how visible it chooses to be to other members.

An individual known to an entrepreneurial network — a founder, mentor or support-organization staff member — with their contact details, the organization they belong to and their memberships, shared between organizations only under the network's consent rules.

A venture's enrollment in a support organization's program, membership or service over a span of time — who provides it, who receives it, the kind of engagement and whether it is applied, active, waitlisted or past — as distinct from single touchpoints.

A structured hand-off of a founder or venture from one support organization to another, tracked from sending through acceptance to an outcome, with a follow-up date and who owns it, so that organizations can see whether introductions actually led anywhere.

A single dated touchpoint between a support organization and someone it serves — a meeting, an email, an event — with its type, who may see it and the notes taken, some of which may be marked confidential.

A long-running piece of work a venture or support organization pursues, tracked against a stage-gate pipeline or checklists, with its current stage, status, start and target dates, and the history of stages it has passed through.
